title: Spice & Wolf
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a medieval-Europe-like world, traveling merchant Kraft Lawrence finds Holo, a centuries-old wolf harvest deity in the form of a girl, hiding in his wagon. Feeling forgotten by farmers who no longer need her blessing, she travels with him toward her northern homeland. Her wit helps his trading schemes, the Church takes an unwelcome interest in her, and the two slowly fall in love.
life_message: A good life is a shared journey of wit, honest bargaining and companionship that outlasts loneliness.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Disputes settled by contracts and bargaining, though Holo's pride as a wisewolf matters.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Itinerant merchant life, free of town and Church control.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Trade relies on guilds and contracts; Holo seeks her homeland kin.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Lawrence and Holo deal as equals despite her divine age.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Farmers' new methods replace the old goddess; rational commerce valued.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Profit and livelihood matter, but the journey's joys matter more.

folkways.japan: Holo's speech is modeled on Edo-period courtesan (oiran) language, and a harvest deity who fades when no longer honored echoes Japanese ideas of kami tied to local worship (Wikipedia).

delivery.evidence: ANN review of vol. 1: economics come through Lawrence's conversational lessons that read naturally; not called preachy

personified.ideology: an old goddess facing being forgotten

delivery.note: Its economic and companionship themes come through dialogue between the leads.

winners_losers: Lawrence and Holo win a partnership; greedy merchants and a controlling Church lose. Sympathy goes to the old goddess and the clever trader.
